# RollingSum: effect of removing the per-tick division

Commit `aa542c6` vs `17066a4`. `on_tick` now compares the timestamp with a cached bucket start, so the division and modulo run only when the bucket changes.

**Result (Intel box):** the average tick is about 36% faster; tail latency is unchanged. The gain is in the common same-bucket tick. Output is identical (regression test passes).

## Average cost

| ns per tick | 10 buckets, old → new | 64 buckets, old → new |
|---|---|---|
| Realistic corpus | 5.15 → 3.26 (−37%) | 5.51 → 3.51 (−36%) |
| Same bucket | 4.87 → 3.28 (−33%) | 4.67 → 3.27 (−30%) |
| Next bucket (gap 1) | 10.74 → 7.44 (−31%) | 7.84 → 5.93 (−24%) |
| Gap of all buckets | 26.27 → 23.27 (−11%) | 74.01 → 78.16 (+6%) |
| Long silence | 5.48 → 5.71 (noise) | 38.84 → 40.88 (+5%) |
| Late tick | 1.70 → 1.21 (−29%) | 1.64 → 1.21 (−26%) |

Corpus: 10 × 1 ms and 64 × 100 µs buckets, where 0.9% and 5.5% of ticks change bucket.

## Tail latency

Each call timed individually on the realistic corpus, net of timer overhead.

| ns per call | 10 × 1 ms, old → new | 64 × 100 µs, old → new |
|---|---|---|
| p50 | below timer resolution | below timer resolution |
| p99 | below timer resolution | 11.69 → 10.02 |
| p99.9 | 11.69 → 13.36 | 36.75 → 41.76 |
| p99.99 | 26.73 → 26.73 | 81.85 → 81.85 |
| max (median of 15) | 687 → 523 | 650 → 638 |

The p99 and p99.9 differences are one to three steps of the 1.67 ns clock, against a timer overhead of 21.7 ns: treat them as flat. The max ranges from about 250 ns to 4,700 ns between samples, so its medians show no real difference.

## Conditions

Intel Core i7-3635QM (Ivy Bridge), g++ 15, `-O2 -march=native`, isolated core 3, fixed 2.4 GHz, Turbo off; median of 15 samples; changes under 5% are noise. Reproduce with `CXX=g++-15 ROUNDS=5 ./bench.sh 17066a4` from `src/feed-handler`.

On the ARM VM (g++ 14) the corpus gained 14% (10 buckets) and 42% (64 buckets), the same-bucket tick was unchanged, and long silence was 16% to 65% slower. Per-call percentiles cannot be measured there (41.67 ns clock step).
